articles.title: Atmane, a raquetazo limpio en la previa de Shanghái y no es expulsado
articles.standfirst: El francés se retiró cuando su rival, Bernard Tomic, sacaba para el partido
articles.summary: El francés se retiró cuando su rival, Bernard Tomic, sacaba para el partido
articles.body: Cuando todavía colea la descalificación de Daniil Medvedev en las semifinales del Open 500 de Pekín, en la previa del Masters 1000 de Shanghái se vio algo peor. El protagonista fue el francés Terence Atmane, el 99 del ranking ATP, en la primera ronda de la fase previa que le midió a Bernard Tomic, el 185 de las listas. El francés no se cansó de tirar la raqueta a cualquier lado de la pista, incluida la grada donde estuvo a punto de impactar en algunos seguidores presentes. Al no impactar ni herir a ninguno de ellos pudo continuar. No contento con eso, Atmane se retiró cuando su rival estaba a punto de sacar para llevarse el partido en el noveno juego del tercer set.

articles.title: Ferrero y su deseo con Alcaraz: "Ya ha pasado un tiempo para que podamos vernos y darnos un abrazo"
articles.standfirst: El exnúmero 1 mundial estrena libro y habla de que se siente listo para volver al circuito
articles.summary: El exnúmero 1 mundial estrena libro y habla de que se siente listo para volver al circuito
articles.body: Juan Carlos Ferrero, 46 años, está de estreno. Desde el miércoles se puede leer Mentalidad ganadora, más allá de la motivación entrena el hábito de la disciplina. El exnúmero 1, que en la actualidad es uno de los entrenadores más reconocidos del circuito, se sienta con MARCA para hablar de su nueva faceta de autor y su futuro en los banquillos. Pregunta. ¿Por qué decide escribir un libro? Respuesta. Quería repasar mi carrera desde que empecé hasta que terminé, y luego el siguiente paso como entrenador. Son dos etapas diferentes, con el mismo denominador común. Para cualquier jugador es bonito recordar las cosas por escrito. Quería aventurarme en algo diferente. He leído bastantes biografías de tenistas y siempre me había atraído la oportunidad de tener la mía. P. En él recuerda lo especial que fue enfrentarse a Andre Agassi en las semifinales del US Open 2003 por ser su ídolo y por el número 1 sobre la mesa. R. Por jugar con mi ídolo y el objetivo que había en juego. Medirte a Agassi siempre era complicado, con el añadido de los seguidores que él tenía allí, jugarnos por el número 1... Superar esas circunstancias hace que sea uno de los partidos que siempre recordaré. P. ¿Cree que tanto Alcaraz como Zverev buscaban en usted que les transmitiera esa experiencia de gran campeón? R. Por supuesto, yo creo que eso ayuda. No quiero decir que si no has sido un jugador no puedes ser un buen entrenador. Pero haber vivido esos momentos te permite dar consejos a tus jugadores para que sepan las dificultades que les puedan venir y saber cómo afrontarlas. P. El prólogo del libro lo hace un gran amigo suyo como Sete Gibernau. ¿Es la persona que más le conoce aparte de su familia? R. Sete me conoce muchísimo. Llevamos ya 26 años de amistad. Desde mis comienzos, compartimos los mismos valores, la misma forma de gestionar las dificultades y eso te acerca mucho más para que la amistad sea más cercana. Era la persona adecuada porque también viajó conmigo a algunos torneos y conocía el circuito desde dentro. P. La última vez que hablamos me comentaba que tenía que pasar el duelo. ¿Qué día se levanta y se dice a sí mismo que ya está listo? R. No es de un día para otro. Sí que va pasando el tiempo y vas abriendo un poquito más el corazón, que se te había cerrado un poquito. Vas sintiendo que puedes volver a ver tenis en la tele, que puedes ver partidos, que ya puedes ver algunos partidos de Carlos, la sensación ya no es la misma. Poco a poco va creciendo esa llama competitiva que como jugador siempre he tenido y ahora surge el pensamiento de querer volver al circuito del tenis el año que viene o cuando sea. P. ¿No es seguro que le veamos en los banquillos en 2027? R. No es seguro al cien por cien porque todavía no tengo nada cerrado. Me gustaría empezar el año que viene, pero todavía no tengo el jugador. P. De las ofertas que ha tenido, ¿le ha sorprendido alguna en especial? R. Sí y no, al final son ofertas que puedes llegar a esperar por la experiencia que tienes como entrenador. He tenido llamadas de todo tipo y es de agradecer que la gente se acuerde. P. Me dijo que prefiere un proyecto de un tenista ya hecho y no tanto uno en formación. R. Digamos que no de 15 años otra vez. Prefiero un jugador que esté en el circuito, pero que, a la vez, tenga margen de maniobra. Es importante entrar en un equipo con el conocimiento de que puedes ser útil. Con el jugador o jugadora que me comprometa espero sentir eso. P. En Italia se mueren de ganas de verle en el banquillo de Jannik Sinner. ¿Es consciente de ello? R. No, no tanto. Sí que es verdad que últimamente no he visto mucho, pero sí que he escuchado cosas. He escuchado a mucha gente que dice, sobre todo los seguidores de Carlos, que sería algo malo si fuera entrenador de Jannik. Al final tienen que entender que en mi carrera, si quiero evolucionar, yo intentaré estar con jugadores interesantes y que puedan darme a mí esa motivación e ilusión de seguir adelante. Si algún día es Jannik espero que lo entiendan y no se lo tomen como si fuera una traición mía hacia Carlos, que no es ni mucho menos mi intención. P. De los perfiles de los tenistas que hay, ¿Sinner es el que más le encajaría porque se va Darren Cahill, por las semanas que tendría que viajar, por el estilo de jugador...? R. No lo sé. Las oportunidades vienen cuando vienen y, si te puedes adaptar a ellas, pues mejor. Lo que puedo asegurar es que no tengo claro con quién voy a entrenar. Sí que podría encajar con Sinner, al igual que con otros, por cómo es, la forma que tiene de estar en pista, pero no sé cuándo va a ser. P. Con Samuel López sigue teniendo trato porque viene a la academia. ¿Hablan mucho de Carlos? R. Sí que le he ido preguntando por el tema de la lesión, en especial. Con Samuel somos socios y amigos desde la infancia, ha sido mi entrenador y eso es algo que va a estar para siempre. El contacto sigue ahí. P. ¿Le gustaría quedar un día con Alcaraz para ir a jugar a golf como antes? R. Me gustaría. Ya ha pasado un tiempo para que podamos vernos tranquilamente y darnos un abrazo. El día que llegue, sí que sería algo positivo para los dos y tarde o temprano tiene que pasar. Va a pasar. P. Mucha gente habla de la irrupción de Rafa Jódar. ¿Le ve potencial para ganar títulos de Grand Slam? R. Me gusta mucho la evolución que está teniendo y el hambre que muestra. En cada partido, cuando le ves ganar, ese sentimiento de victoria... Me está gustando mucho, ha mejorado y ha evolucionado y seguro que el año que viene va a ser importante para él. P. Sin Sinner, lesionado, ¿es el año para que Alcaraz gane las ATP Finals y la Copa Davis? R. Carlos ha mejorado mucho en cuanto llega a final de temporada. El año pasado estuvo cerca. El partido con Jannik fue muy parejo y al final se le escapó. Sin Jannik, Carlos es uno de los principales favoritos junto con Zverev. Carlos llega muy fresco por las circunstancias y le veo con muchas posibilidades. P. Usted estuvo como entrenador de Sascha. ¿Se ha alegrado de que finalmente rompiera esa barrera en los grandes? R. Mucho. Porque creo que es bueno para el tenis. Es el momento en el que él puede dar un paso adelante y disputarles los Grand Slam tanto a Jannik como a Carlos. Es un jugador que ha madurado, que está haciendo las cosas mejor y que se ha dado cuenta de que evolucionar es una de las grandes motivaciones que puede tener un tenista y que realmente lo tienes que hacer. El deporte no corre sino vuela. La gente evoluciona muy rápido y él se ha dado cuenta. Y no es tarde para que siga compitiendo de tú a tú. Allí están los resultados que ha tenido. P. En la mesa del tenis se debate la posibilidad de reducir a cuatro juegos los sets en los cuatro grandes o que los partidos sean al mejor de tres mangas. ¿Cuál es su opinión al respecto? R. Yo creo que es una cosa que va a llegar pero no sé cuándo. Igual que llegó en los Masters 1000, cuando se quitaron las finales a cinco sets, o en las finales de los 500. Es algo que haría perder un poquito de esencia, ya la perdió en la Copa Davis y nos hemos ido quejando porque lo vemos muy diferente y nos pasará lo mismo con los Grand Slam. Pero a nivel físico es algo que importa de cara a las carreras de futuro de los jugadores y en algún momento va a pasar. Lo que no estoy seguro es si me va a gustar porque es algo nuevo y al jugador los cinco sets siempre los hemos sentido como una forma especial de jugar un torneo, diferente a los otros.

articles.title: Zverev survives small scare to reach Shanghai Masters second round
articles.summary: Germany's Alexander Zverev survived a brief scare on Friday to advance to the third round of the Shanghai Masters, beating Wu Yibing 6-4, 7-6 (7-4). Zverev w...
articles.body:
Germany's Alexander Zverev survived a brief scare on Friday to advance to the third round of the Shanghai Masters, beating Wu Yibing 6-4, 7-6 (7-4).

Zverev was leading 6-4, 5-5 and had a break point on Wu's serve when he stumbled out wide after striking a backhand.

He seemed to have tweaked his left ankle, but after a brief break, he was able to move with relative freedom in the closing stages of the match.

Zverev can reach year-end number one spot in the men's world rakings in Shanghai if he reaches the semi-finals. He's currently world number two behind Jannik Sinner, who ended his season early due to knee issues.

The German has won the French Open and the US Open this year and is bidding for his first Masters title since 2024.

articles.title: Cuándo es el Alcaraz - Cerúndolo: fecha, horario y dónde ver en TV el debut de Carlos en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái
articles.standfirst: El flamante campeón de Tokio se estrenará este sábado con el argentino, verdugo de Nicolás Mejía
articles.summary: El flamante campeón de Tokio se estrenará este sábado con el argentino, verdugo de Nicolás Mejía
articles.body: Sin tiempo para muchas celebraciones, Carlos Alcaraz ya se encuentra en Shanghái para preparar el penúltimo Masters 1000 del calendario, que se perdió la pasada campaña por fatiga. De esta forma, el murciano tiene la opción de sumar 1.000 puntos que le asienten en el 'top3' mundial y le acerquen al objetivo de recuperar el número 1 ATP la temporada que viene. Alcaraz ya sabe que se estrenará este sábado 10 de octubre con Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, el 55 del ranking ATP, y verdugo de Nicolás Mejia, el 119 y procedente de la fase previa. El único precedente entre ambos cayó del lado del fenómeno de El Palmar en el 'round robin' de las Next Gen Finals de Milán, en 2021. Carlitos acabaría por levantar el trofeo. Carlos Alcaraz disputará su primer partido en el TMS asiático este sábado 10 de octubre, en la central del Qu Zhong, sobre las 12.00 del mediodía, hora peninsular. El primer partido de Carlos Alcaraz en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái, con Juan Manuel Cerúndolo de adversario, podrá seguirse en España a través de Movistar+, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Davidovich arrolla a Brooksby en Shanghái
articles.standfirst: Se medirá ahora a Frances Tiafoe en tercera ronda
articles.summary: Se medirá ahora a Frances Tiafoe en tercera ronda
articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich se clasificó para la tercera ronda del Másters 1000 de Shanghái al vencer con claridad al estadounidense Jenson Brooksby (6-1 y 6-3) que llegó a esta duelo tras haber ganado antes a Jaume Munar. El primer set siguió prácticamente el mismo desarrollo que en el partido de Munar que, como esta vez Davidovich, se puso 5-1 por delante. El malagueño sí pudo mantener la renta e evitar que esta vez Brooksby remontara como ante el mallorquín. En la segunda manga, la igualdad y los intercambios de golpes duraron hasta el séptimo juego. Otro break a favor de Davidovich le permitió sellar una victoria sencilla en una hora y 12 minutos. El duelo sirvió también para desempatar el balance entre ambos contendientes: Brooksby se había llevado la victoria en Amberes 2021, y Davidovich le devolvió la jugada en Basilea en 2025. El español afrontará ahora un duro duelo ante el séptimo cabeza de serie del torneo, el estadounidense Frances Tiafoe, que se deshizo del alemán Yannick Hanfmann (6-4, 6-4).

articles.title: Wimbledon boss jokes Royal Marines would 'love to sort out' disruptive influencers
articles.summary: Royal Marine Commandos providing security at Wimbledon would like "nothing more than to sort out" disruptive social media influencers at the prestigious tournament, its chief executive jokes.
articles.body:
Royal Marine commandos providing security at Wimbledon would like "nothing more than to sort out" disruptive social media influencers at the prestigious tournament, its chief executive has joked.

US Open organisers accredited 100 influencers and content creators for this year's tournament.

But when a match involving two-time champion Naomi Osaka was disrupted by a group of influencers conducting a photo shoot, it prompted a debate about tennis etiquette.

Richard Atkinson, interim chief executive at the All England Lawn Tennis Club, said Wimbledon did not offer accreditation to influencers and sources have indicated to BBC Sport that is unlikely to change in the near future.

While Atkinson acknowledged that influencers were a "crucial part of the marketing mix" and to ban them from attending the tournament entirely would be "nonsense", he said any that were brought in by brands would be "tightly chaperoned".

He also backed the traditional "self-policing" ethos at SW19, whereby fans respect the action.

After the disruption at the US Open, world number four Coco Gauff said it was important to welcome a "new demographic" to the sport, but said: "I think it's just, follow the etiquette of the sport. That's all."

And Wimbledon's boss made it clear he does not expect to see a repeat at the All England Club.

"We don't have a category of accredited people called influencers," Atkinson told a panel at Leaders Week London.

"That said, clearly influencers are a crucial part of building your brand around the world in the third decade of the 21st century.

"What you have to do is keep them under control. One of our big partners, Polo Ralph Lauren, will have their influencer, but they are all tightly chaperoned."

He said the atmosphere at the US Open is "very New York City", adding: "It's dead easy for someone who has just bought a ticket to show up there with their ring lights and literally start broadcasting in the middle of a match.

"If you tried to do that at Wimbledon, I think you'd probably have some Royal Marine Commando…"

He then joked: "We do have military. And they would like nothing more, I suspect, than to sort out some influencer."

Fans will also not be allowed to bring portable ring lights - a piece of equipment used by content creators - to SW19.

Atkinson did, however, point out that the media landscape has changed, and suggested there is a place for embracing influencers and content creators to ensure Wimbledon remains relevant.

"It's just a crucial bit of the marketing mix, of course it is," he said.

"We're not in the world of newspapers and television anymore, right? The world has changed. But it's just really important, it's a bit of a cliched expression, you've got to sort it out in a Wimbledon way. But to say "we're not going to have any influencers at Wimbledon", it's obviously nonsense."

"Our marketing team work meticulously to make sure they are working in a way that is consistent with our Wimbledon brand and keeps that magic that I was referring to earlier."

images.caption: Image caption, Wimbledon's boss said the SW19 crowd is 'self-policing' when it comes to behaviour

articles.title: Djokovic se despide de Shanghái y no puede celebrar con victoria su récord en los Masters 1000
articles.standfirst: Hurkacz vence por 6-4 y 6-3 a un Novak con problemas en el partido en el que se convirtió en el tenista con más participaciones en un torneo de esta categoría
articles.summary: Vence a Hurkacz por X-x y X-x en el encuentro que le permite ser el tenista con más participaciones en un torneo de este nivel con 140
articles.body: Novak Djokovic cayó ante Hubert Hurkacz en su estreno en esta edición del Masters 1000 de Shanghái. Tras levantar su título número 102 en Pekín, el serbio, al que se le vio excesivamente cansado, perdió por 4-6 y 3-6 en un encuentro en el que se convirtió en el tenista con más participaciones en un torneo de esta categoría desde su creación en 1990. Llega a las 140 y supera a Feliciano López con el que compartía el tope de 139. Suma así un registro más a su larga lista de récords, entre los que destacan el que más Masters 1000 ha ganado con 40 y el único que ha levantado el trofeo de todos ellos en dos ocasiones. Djokovic se enfrentó a un partido exigente con puntos largos. En varias ocasiones se puso en cuclillas entre juego y juego para coger aire. Le costaba respirar como le suele ocurrir cuando el calor y la humedad están presentes. En el tercer juego del primer set dispuso de dos opciones de break, pero Hurkacz las salvó. Cuando Novak se marchó hacia la silla, el juez le dio un toque por los gritos de Viktor Troicki, desde el box de su equipo técnico, durante este punto. Con 5-4 a favor el polaco dispuso de dos pelotas de set. La primera, con el segundo servicio de Novak, la desaprovechó con un error no forzado al mandar la bola al pasillo de dobles. La segunda, en idénticas circunstancias, sí la rentabilizó con un resto ganador. Entre set y set, desde el box le hicieron llegar a Novak un gel y un termo con batido para hacer frente a sus temblores. El partido siguió el mismo guion. Djokovic, incómodo en la pista, se dejó su servicio con una doble falta en el cuarto juego. Hurkacz no aflojó. La presión de estar cerca de ganar por primera vez a 'Nole' en su carrera no le pasó factura. El campeón de 24 grand slams dio una vez más muestras de su compromiso con su deporte. Cualquier otro hubiera arrojado la toalla en una situación similar. Levantó dos bolas de break con 4-1 en contra para deleite del público. Alargó el set que finalmente cerraría el polaco con un 6-3 para meterse en tercera ronda y acabar con la presencia de Djokovic en Shanghái. "Si pierdes tu servicio, basta con perder el partido, una vez por set, y eso fue lo que pasó. Es muy difícil devolver su servicio, casi imposible. Así que sí, no me adapté y fue un sorteo muy complicado para mí, jugar contra él en el primer partido", analizó Djokovic. Desveló también que en su calendario tiene fijado sólo el Masters 1000 de París y que espera poder clasificarse para las ATP Finals.

images.caption: Djokovic, tras caer ante Hurkacz en Shanghái. EFE
Djokovic, durante su partido ante Hurkacz. LAPRESSE

articles.title: Novak Djokovic knocked out of Shanghai Masters in second round as Britain's Arthur Fery also beaten
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic, who won the China Open on Tuesday for the 102nd title of his career, goes down 6-4 6-3 to Hubert Hurkacz in his Shanghai opener; Arthur Fery beaten by 26th seed Karen Khachanov in epic three-setter; top seed Alexander Zverev through to third round
articles.body:
Djokovic was on a high coming into the tournament after claiming a seventh China Open title - and the 102nd of his career - on Tuesday, although he didn't have to win a match point in either the semi-final or final.

Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from their final-four clash after hitting a spectator with the ball , while Alex De Minaur retired hurt after dropping the first set of the final, ⁠with Djokovic leading 7-6 (7-3) 0-1.

The 39-year-old was far from his best when in his Shanghai opener on Friday, beaten in straight sets - 6-4 6-3 - by Hurkacz.

It's Djokovic's first career defeat to the Pole, having won their prior eight encounters. But the former world No 6 produced a ‌clinical display, sending down 13 aces and 28 winners while conceding little on serve to defeat the 24-time Grand Slam champion.

The defeat marked the latest setback in a testing season for the Serbian, who suffered a shock first-round exit at the US Open, his earliest Grand Slam ​defeat since the 2006 Australian Open.

"I was not close to what I was playing in Beijing," Djokovic said. "I'm ⁠slightly more tired, not fresh.

"I didn't feel myself on the court ⁠in terms of feeling the ball. It's a super quick surface, completely different from Beijing.

"If you lose your serve, it is enough to lose the match, once per set, and that is ‌what happened. It is very difficult to return his serve, almost impossible. So yeah, I did not adjust and it was a really tough draw for me, playing him in the first match."

Djokovic will now turn his attention to the European indoor swing, with next month's ‌Paris Masters looming. He is ninth in the race for a spot at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin.

"I am planning on only playing in Paris, so let's see. Hopefully I can have a good result there," he said.

Britain's Arthur Fery also exits at the second-round stage, after losing out in an epic match with 26th seed Karen Khachanov that lasted over three and a half hours - all three sets decided by a tie-break.

Fery lost his opening service game of the match, but broke back to send the opening set to a tie-break, which Khachanov claimed 8-6.

Roles were reversed in the second, as the Wimbledon semi-finalist took the breaker 7-5, while it appeared to be advantage Fery in the decider when 4-2 and a break up.

However Khachanov battled back and took the final tie-break 7-2 to secure his spot in the third round.

Top seed Zverev secures safe passage to third round

Top seed Alexander Zverev got his tournament off to a winning start, as this year's two-time major winner beat Chinese wildcard entry Wu Yibing 6-4 7-6 (7-4).

US Open runner-up Ben Shelton - beaten by Zverev in his first Grand Slam final - celebrated his 24th birthday with a 6-3 7-6 (8-6) win over Daniel Altmaier.

It represented a return to winning ways for the American after losing both of his singles matches for the United States in the Davis Cup following on from his run to the final at Flushing Meadows.

Ninth seed Alex de Minaur advanced with a walkover after his opponent, Alex Molcan, retired with an undisclosed ailment. De Minaur himself had to retire with an adductor injury in the China Open final against Djokovic on Tuesday.

Mertens stuns Swiatek in Beijing, sets up China Open semi-final with Zheng

Elise Mertens stunned former champion Iga Swiatek 7-6 (7-0) 6-3 to ‌reach the China Open semi-finals, continuing her impressive run in Beijing after also eliminating ‌American third seed Coco Gauff earlier in the week.

The 30-year-old Belgian, ranked ​19th in the world, produced a composed display to secure victory.

Her path has been anything but easy, as she has defeated three consecutive Grand Slam champions: Jelena Ostapenko, Coco Gauff and now Swiatek to advance to just the third WTA ‌1000 semi-final of her career and her first since 2021.

She ⁠will next face home favourite Qinwen Zheng , who defeated sixth seed Elina Svitolina 6-3 7-6 (8-6) earlier in the day to book ‌her place in the last four.

"She's an incredible player. She's been a top 10 player," Mertens said. "Of course, [she was] unlucky with the injury, but her level is there. It's going to be a great match. She has a home advantage, but still I'm enjoying my time here in Beijing. I'm still in singles and doubles. I'm going to give 100 per cent again."

articles.title: Novak Djokovic suffers surprise loss to Hubert Hurkacz at Shanghai Masters
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic suffers a surprise second-round loss to Hubert Hurkacz at the Shanghai Masters, just three days after his triumph at the China Open in Beijing.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic suffered a surprise second-round loss to Hubert Hurkacz at the Shanghai Masters, just three days after triumphing at the China Open in Beijing.

The 39-year-old Djokovic ended an 11-month wait to lift the 102nd title of his illustrious career after Alex de Minaur retired injured from the China Open final.

But, contesting his sixth match in the space of 10 days, Djokovic lost to Hurkacz for the first time in nine career meetings with the Pole.

The big-serving Hurkacz, winner in 2023 and currently ranked 34th in the world, claimed a 6-4 6-3 victory in 87 minutes.

"It's a special night. I've been playing Novak for like seven years. It's been unsuccessful but [he has been] such a great champion for so many years," Hurkacz said.

"He just won Beijing, so it's a very difficult task to play against him, but also it is a pleasure for me to share a court with him, to play such a legend of the sport."

Men's record 24-time Grand Slam champion Djokovic claimed a tour-level singles title for the 21st year in a row with his victory in Beijing, where he is on a 34-match winning streak.

That was only his second final of the year following January's Australian Open final defeat by Carlos Alcaraz.

But, having beaten world number two Alexander Zverev and led third seed Daniil Medvedev by a set and a break when the Russian was defaulted on his way to the Beijing final, Djokovic's Shanghai bid as undone by a single break of serve in both sets against Hurkacz.

While victory in Beijing boosted his hopes of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals, Djokovic, currently ninth in the race to Turin, will now require a strong showing at the Paris Masters in November to break into the top eight.

Also in Shanghai, Great Britain's Arthur Fery lost out in a closely-fought three-set contest against former top-10 player Karen Khachanov.

Fery, who achieved a fairytale run to the Wimbledon semi-finals this year, was beaten 7-6 (8-6) 6-7 (5-7) 7-6 (7-2) after three-and-a-half hours.

articles.title: Coco Gauff Stars in Gunna's Music Video for New Single 'Pop It'
articles.summary: Having already reached the top of the tennis world at the age of 22, Coco Gauff is venturing into the entertainment field.
articles.body:
Having already reached the top of the tennis world at the age of 22, Coco Gauff is venturing into the entertainment field.

Gauff is featured prominently in the music video for Gunna's new single "Pop It" that dropped on Friday.

The video features Gauff playing with Gunna on the tennis court, with additional sequences featuring helicopter shots over California and a gathering at a mansion surrounded by sports cars.

Gunna's song is his first solo single release of the year ahead of the anticipated release of his next album Splurge .

Gauff most recently competed in the China Open, losing to Elise Mertens in the fourth round. She previously won the U.S. Open in 2023 and French Open in 2025.

articles.title: Jessica Pegula’s tennis career is only part of her family story: Inside her relationship with Taylor Gahagen to life away from the court and more
articles.summary: Explore the inspiring life of Jessica Pegula, a top American tennis player, as she navigates her successful career, close relationship with husband Taylor Gahagen, and meaningful contributions to philanthropy and entrepreneurship.
articles.body: Jessica Pegula is one of the best American players of her generation. But she’s so much more than tournament wins and WTA rankings. Pegula, a Buffalo, New York native, is the daughter of Terry and Kim Pegula, owners of the Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres, and comes from a family with deep roots in professional sports. She has made a career out of her own exploits on the tennis circuit.Away from competition, Pegula has also built a life with Taylor Gahagen, a businessman who has remained a close and largely private presence throughout her rise. Their relationship began years before their marriage, and Gahagen has since become involved in several aspects of Pegula’s life, including her business interests and philanthropic work. Their partnership has developed alongside Pegula’s demanding international tennis schedule.Details on Jessica Pegula and Taylor Gahagen’s relationship, marriage and life beyond tennisJessica Pegula and Taylor Gahagen first became linked publicly around 2015. Their relationship developed while Gahagen was working for Pegula Sports and Entertainment, the organisation associated with Pegula’s parents. Gahagen had already established a career in the sports-business environment, giving the pair a professional connection before their relationship became a significant part of their personal lives.The couple became engaged by early 2019 and initially planned to marry in 2020. Those plans were delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, eventually pushing their wedding back by a year. In October 2021, Pegula and Gahagen finally married at the Biltmore Estate in Asheville, North Carolina, surrounded by family, friends and several members of Pegula’s tennis circle.Their marriage has remained relatively private compared with the public attention surrounding Pegula’s professional career. Gahagen is regularly described as an important support figure, travelling with Pegula when possible while maintaining his own professional responsibilities away from the tennis spotlight. The couple also eventually found time for a honeymoon in Costa Rica in 2022, after Pegula’s demanding playing schedule made immediate travel difficult.Taylor Gahagen supports Jessica Pegula’s tennis journeyGahagen’s role in Pegula’s life goes beyond that of a spouse, and his background in business and sports management has given him an understanding of the pressures surrounding professional athletics. Before moving into other ventures, he worked for nearly a decade at Pegula Sports and Entertainment, where he held several positions before becoming an executive. He left the organisation in 2023 and later became a managing partner at Dragos Capital and Agarwood Wealth.His support has also been visible around Pegula’s tennis career, and with tournaments requiring constant travel, training and preparation, having a trusted person nearby can provide stability away from competition. Pegula has spoken about having a strong support system, while reports have highlighted Gahagen’s presence around her during major events.Pegula’s tennis résumé has continued to grow during their marriage. The WTA lists her career-high singles ranking as No 3 and records multiple WTA singles titles, including victories in Charleston and Dubai in 2026. She has also enjoyed substantial success in doubles, including titles with Coco Gauff.The relationship has therefore developed alongside some of the biggest stages of Pegula’s career. Rather than becoming a highly publicised celebrity partnership, Pegula and Gahagen have generally kept their personal life understated while allowing their professional achievements to remain the focus.Jessica Pegula balances family, business and philanthropyPegula’s family background remains another major part of her story. Her parents, Terry and Kim Pegula, became prominent figures in American professional sports through their ownership of the Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres. That connection has naturally placed Pegula under additional attention, but her tennis career has developed independently through years of training and competition.Her family life has also included difficult periods, and Kim Pegula experienced a serious health crisis in 2022, and Jessica later discussed the impact of her mother’s condition while continuing to compete at the highest level. The experience added another dimension to Pegula’s public story, demonstrating the challenge of balancing major family circumstances with the demands of professional tennis.Outside tennis, Pegula has developed entrepreneurial interests. She founded Ready 24, a skincare company designed around active lifestyles, with Gahagen also involved in the venture. The brand focuses on straightforward skincare products for people with demanding or active routines. Gahagen has served as vice president of the company, giving the couple another professional project alongside their personal relationship.Their philanthropic work has become another important part of their life away from tennis. Pegula and Gahagen co-founded A Lending Paw, an organisation focused on helping rescue dogs receive training that can prepare them to become service animals for people in need. The initiative reflects their shared interest in animal welfare while connecting rescued animals with people who require assistance.The organisation has continued to attract outside support. In 2026, The Farmer’s Dog announced a multi-year partnership supporting A Lending Paw’s mission to help more rescue dogs receive care, nutrition and training before becoming service animals. Pegula has also been identified as the owner of three rescue dogs, Maddie, Des and Mabel, reinforcing the personal connection behind the initiative.Pegula’s life away from tennis consequently combines family, entrepreneurship and philanthropy rather than simply revolving around her status as a professional athlete. Her marriage to Gahagen is an important part of that balance, particularly because their shared projects allow their professional and charitable interests to overlap.While tennis remains the centre of Pegula’s public career, her wider story has continued to develop in parallel. Her relationship with Gahagen has provided a private foundation during an increasingly demanding period of competition, while their work through Ready 24 and A Lending Paw has given them shared interests outside sport.Pegula’s family connections may have introduced her to the world of professional sports from an early age, but her achievements have been shaped by her own career. Her rise to a career-high No 3 ranking, WTA titles and deep runs at major tournaments have established her as a significant figure in American tennis.Together, these elements show why Pegula’s story cannot be reduced to tennis alone, and her marriage, family experiences, business interests and charitable commitments provide a broader picture of an athlete building a life both within and beyond professional competition.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Days after China Open triumph, Djokovic suffers first-ever loss to Hurkacz in career-earliest Shanghai exit
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic exits the Shanghai Masters earlier than ever after facing Hubert Hurkacz, suffering his first defeat against the Polish player just days after winning the China Open. Djokovic reveals his plans for the rest of the season amid concerns over his qualification for the ATP Finals.
articles.body: Novak Djokovic arrived in Shanghai riding the momentum of another title-winning week, but his stay at the Masters event ended far sooner than he would have hoped. Just days after lifting his 102nd career trophy in Beijing, the 39-year-old suffered his first-ever defeat against Hubert Hurkacz, and the result has now prompted the Serbian to reveal his plans for the remainder of the season.Djokovic suffers earliest-ever Shanghai Masters exitDjokovic lost 6-4, 6-3 to Hurkacz in the second round on Friday, October 9, ending a run of eight consecutive victories against the Polish player. The four-time Shanghai champion struggled to find his rhythm against Hurkacz's powerful serve, with the world No. 34 securing victory in 87 minutes after breaking Djokovic once in each set.The defeat also marked Djokovic's earliest-ever exit from the Shanghai Masters, where he received a first-round bye as the 10th seed.Hurkacz, who won the Shanghai title in 2023, acknowledged the significance of finally beating one of tennis's greatest players after years of unsuccessful attempts.“It's a special night. I've been playing Novak for like seven years. It's been unsuccessful but [he has been] such a great champion for so many years,” Hurkacz said.“He just won Beijing, so it's a very difficult task to play against him, but also it is a pleasure for me to share a court with him, to play such a legend of the sport.”Djokovic had little time to recover after his China Open triumph, having played six matches in nine days during a demanding run that included victories over three top-10 opponents on his way to the Beijing title.Djokovic explains what went wrong against HurkaczSpeaking after the defeat, Djokovic admitted that the match had proved difficult, particularly because Hurkacz gave him very few opportunities to put pressure on his serve.“Beijing was great and a very early exit here but it is ok,” Djokovic said. “I had a great week in Beijing and I look forward to resting a little bit and get ready for the indoors.”The Serbian also explained how the match turned on a small number of crucial points, with a single break in each set enough for Hurkacz to take control.“If you lose your serve, it is enough to lose the match, once per set, and that is what happened,” Djokovic said.“It is very difficult to return his serve, almost impossible. So yeah, I did not adjust and it was a really tough draw for me, playing him in the first match.”Djokovic had arrived in Shanghai after capturing his seventh China Open title, extending his unbeaten record in Beijing to 34 matches. His latest triumph also made him a tour-level singles champion for the 21st consecutive year, adding another milestone to an already extraordinary career.The Beijing title was his 102nd at tour level, coming after Alex de Minaur retired injured from the final. It was also only his second final of the season, following his runner-up finish at the Australian Open in February.Djokovic confirms Paris Masters as his next tournamentDjokovic has now indicated that he plans to rest before returning to competition at the Paris Masters in November, rather than adding further tournaments to his schedule before the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin.“I would like to [play the Nitto ATP Finals]. I am planning on only playing in Paris, so let’s see,” Djokovic said. “Hopefully I can have a good result there.”The Serbian currently sits ninth in the race to Turin, leaving him outside the top eight places required to qualify for the ATP Finals. A strong showing in Paris could therefore prove decisive as he attempts to secure another appearance at the season-ending tournament.The Paris Masters main draw begins on November 2, giving Djokovic approximately 25 days away from ATP Tour competition following his Shanghai exit.Despite the early defeat, Djokovic can take considerable confidence from his Beijing performance, where he defeated Alexander Zverev and progressed past Daniil Medvedev after leading the Russian by a set and a break before Medvedev was defaulted.For now, his priority is recovery, with the Paris Masters offering the next opportunity to improve his position in the race to Turin and finish the season strongly.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: COVID-19 hero: How Novak Djokovic donated €1 million during one of mankind’s worst crises— the ventilators, CT scanners and medical equipment his money helped buy
articles.summary: Explore how Novak Djokovic and his wife, Jelena, donated €1 million for ventilators and medical equipment during the COVID-19 pandemic and how their foundation continues to support children's early education in Serbia.
articles.body: “I am very proud to be an athlete in these times, among many greats who have come forward to bring people together at a time when we are apart,” Novak Djokovic said in 2020, as the COVID-19 pandemic strained healthcare systems around the world. In Serbia, Djokovic and his wife, Jelena, donated €1 million to help hospitals obtain ventilators, clinical monitors and CT scanners. It was a moment when the influence of sport reached far beyond the court, as athletes around the world began asking what they could do in a crisis that had brought everyday life to a standstill. For Djokovic, the donation would become part of a much wider effort, one that drew in corporate partners and individual donors and raised a further US$200,000 in support.What Djokovic's €1 million helped buy during COVID-19When the pandemic disrupted everyday life in March 2020, the Novak Djokovic Foundation had to rethink how it supported children, parents and educators, but the pressure on Serbia's hospitals created another immediate need that the couple felt they could not ignore.Novak and Jelena made global headlines when they personally donated €1 million, around US$1.12 million at the time, to help Serbia’s hospitals get the equipment they desperately needed.They were among many athletes, celebrities and public figures who stepped up during the pandemic, but Djokovic wanted to make sure his contribution went where it could do the most good. To figure that out, he reached out to people around the world for advice on how best to get help to those who needed itThe foundation's team then worked to identify the equipment hospitals required, making sure deliveries arrived as quickly as possible while meeting quality standards and the needs of individual healthcare institutions. Its 2020 review recorded 17 ventilators, 54 clinical monitors, two high-quality CT scanners, mobile equipment for disinfecting surfaces and syringe pumps among the items delivered during the year.The foundation also distributed 100,000 health packages to first-graders across Serbia, while directing more than €40,000 towards the General Hospital in Novi Pazar when the town faced a particularly difficult period during the pandemic. Ventilators and monitors also formed part of the support provided to hospitals, including a contribution to the General Hospital in Kruševac.Djokovic explained why he felt athletes had a responsibility to help when communities were struggling during the crisis, expressing admiration for those who used their visibility and resources to bring people together.“I am very proud to be an athlete in these times, among many greats who have come forward to bring people together at a time when we are apart—to bring hope, community, and inspire others in the same way to use our platforms for good.”The couple's contribution became the starting point for a wider relief effort, with corporate partners and individual supporters providing a further US$200,000 worth of donations. Overall, pandemic assistance channelled through the foundation exceeded €1.2 million, with documented medical equipment deliveries valued at more than €1.023 million.The pandemic changed their work, but not their missionThe Novak Djokovic Foundation was established to improve children's lives in Serbia, with early childhood education becoming its central mission as Novak and Jelena recognised how many children lacked access to quality preschool learning. Their work had already produced tangible results before the pandemic, with the foundation opening its thirteenth School of Life in Ljukovo at the beginning of 2020. The new preschool created 96 places for children aged three to six in an area where more than 200 children had been waiting for enrolment.When COVID-19 disrupted everyday life, however, the foundation had to pause much of its in-person work, including planned preschool projects, while the couple remained committed to helping children, parents and teachers. Rather than wait for normality to return, the team moved educational programmes and parenting workshops online, giving families access to learning materials and practical advice during lockdown.Construction work resumed as restrictions eased, while the foundation continued preparing new preschools and supporting families through its existing programmes. The pandemic changed how the organisation worked, but its purpose remained the same: helping children from vulnerable backgrounds access the care, education and opportunities they needed to develop.Why Djokovic and Jelena built their foundation around childrenThe pandemic response was possible because the couple already had an organisation with experience in supporting vulnerable communities, having established the Novak Djokovic Foundation in 2007 before eventually concentrating its resources on early childhood education.The foundation initially provided broad humanitarian assistance in Serbia, supporting schools, churches and families facing poverty or illness, but a meeting with UNICEF in 2012 helped Novak and Jelena identify a more specific problem they wanted to address.They learned that more than half of Serbian children were not attending preschool or other early education programmes, while participation in the poorest rural communities fell below 10 per cent. Many children therefore started primary school without access to the learning opportunities, facilities and support that could help them develop alongside their peers.Both Novak and Jelena had grown up in economically difficult, war-affected Serbia during the 1990s, and Novak has often acknowledged how fortunate he was to have a family that supported his ambitions from an early age. They wanted other children to have comparable opportunities, regardless of their family's financial circumstances or where they happened to live.The foundation consequently made early childhood development its central mission, concentrating on the period from birth to age seven, when learning and development can shape a child's later opportunities. Its motto, “Believe in their dreams”, reflects the idea that children should have the support to discover their abilities rather than have their futures restricted by circumstances beyond their control.How the foundation's work has grown beyond emergency reliefThe couple's work has since continued to centre on early education, with the foundation building or reconstructing 58 preschools and investing more than €15 million in programmes that have positively affected over 55,000 children.Its wider work includes training teachers, helping municipalities transform unused buildings into preschools, supporting parents through workshops and digital resources, and collaborating with organisations including UNICEF, the World Bank and Harvard University's Center on the Developing Child.The foundation also relies on public support to expand these programmes, while Novak and Jelena cover administrative and operational expenses personally or through an endowment, allowing public donations to go directly towards programme delivery.Even during the difficult year of 2020, the couple continued matching public generosity with their own contributions. The foundation's annual Season of Giving campaign collected €108,000 (~$140,000) from more than 1,000 supporters across over 30 countries, after which Novak and Jelena matched the amount to create a total of €216,000 (~$280,000) for new preschools in the Serbian villages of Vajska and Ljubis, helping provide early education for 105 children.The pandemic donation remains one of the clearest examples of how that work can extend beyond the foundation's usual focus, with the couple using an established organisation to direct emergency assistance towards hospitals while keeping their longer-term educational commitments moving. For Djokovic, the €1 million contribution was not a separate philanthropic gesture detached from his other work, but part of a wider effort to give children and families in Serbia access to the support they need during both ordinary times and major crises.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rafa Jódar se estrena con victoria en Shanghái y se mantiene en la pelea por estar en las ATP Finals de Turín
articles.standfirst: El madrileño derrota al argentino Tirante en tres apretados sets y se las verá con Lehecka
articles.summary: El madrileño derrota al argentino Tirante en tres apretados sets y se las verá con Lehecka
articles.body: Rafa Jódar ha celebrado con victoria en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái su nueva asociación con la marca de relojes Rolex. El madrileño, de tan sólo 20 años, se ha clasificado este sábado para la tercera ronda del certamen chino tras acabar con la resistencia de Tiago Tirante, por 4-6, 6-2 y 6-3, en algo más de dos horas. Para encontrar su último triunfo en el circuito había que remontarse al 17 de agosto, en la tercera ronda de Cincinnati con el chileno Alejandro Tabilo. Jódar, que venía de perder a la primera en el US Open y Tokio, se mantiene en la pelea por estar en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). Rafa es undécimo de la Race 2026, que da billete a la cita de maestros. Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz y Ben Shelton son los únicos que tienen asegurada su presencia en el 'round robin'. La ausencia de Jannik Sinner en el torneo de final de año por su lesión de rodilla situaría ahora mismo al joven de Tenis Chamartín como reserva. Suma 2.559 puntos, a tan sólo 281 puntos del corte que marca hoy Novak Djokovic. En la siguiente ronda del TMS de Shanghái se las verá con Jiri Lehecka, que viene de alcanzar la final en Tokio ante Alcaraz. Al decimosegundo cabeza de serie del cuadro le restan dos torneos más por disputar: el Open 500 de Basilea y el Masters 1000 de París, con un total de 1.500 puntos en juego. Flavio Cobolli y Djokovic han sido los únicos que no han sumado una sola victoria en Shanghái. El resto de implicados en la pelea por estar en Turín siguen con vida, dígase Frances Tiafoe, Arthur Fils, Daniil Medvedev, Alex de Miñaur y Taylor Fritz.

articles.summary: El flamante campeón de Tokio se estrenará este sábado con el argentino, verdugo de Nicolás Mejía
articles.body: Sin tiempo para muchas celebraciones, Carlos Alcaraz ya se encuentra en Shanghái para preparar el penúltimo Masters 1000 del calendario, que se perdió la pasada campaña por fatiga. De esta forma, el murciano tiene la opción de sumar 1.000 puntos que le asienten en el 'top3' mundial y le acerquen al objetivo de recuperar el número 1 ATP la temporada que viene. Alcaraz ya sabe que se estrenará este sábado 10 de octubre con Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, el 55 del ranking ATP, y verdugo de Nicolás Mejia, el 119 y procedente de la fase previa. El único precedente entre ambos cayó del lado del fenómeno de El Palmar en el 'round robin' de las Next Gen Finals de Milán, en 2021. Carlitos acabaría por levantar el trofeo. Carlos Alcaraz disputará su primer partido en el TMS asiático este sábado 10 de octubre, en la central del Qu Zhong, sobre las 12.00 del mediodía, hora peninsular. El primer partido de Carlos Alcaraz en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái, con Juan Manuel Cerúndolo de adversario, podrá seguirse en España a través de Movistar+, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz y su equipo estrenan look en Shanghái: todos con bigote
articles.standfirst: El murciano debuta este sábado en el Masters 1000 con Juan Manuel Cerúndolo
articles.summary: El murciano debuta este sábado en el Masters 1000 con Juan Manuel Cerúndolo
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz tendrá una nueva imagen este sábado cuando salte a disputar su primer partido en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái contra Juan Manuel Cerúndolo. El murciano, después de una apuesta con los miembros de su equipo, estrena un look innovador con bigote que han tenido que seguir el resto de sus acompañantes. El campeón de siete grandes lucía su nueva imagen en el calentamiento previo al duelo con el pequeño de la familia Cerúndolo. También aparecían con bigote su entrenador, Samuel López; su hermano Álvaro; su preparador y fisioterapeuta, Juanjo Moreno, y su agente Albert Molina. Todo viene de la celebración tras la consecución del título de Tokio en la que el fisio del tenista gritó: "Bigotes para todos". Dicho y hecho. No es la primera vez que Carlitos y su cuerpo técnico cruzan una apuesta que luego se tiene que pagar. El año pasado tuvieron que teñirse de rubio tras la consecución del US Open. Su cambio de look más radical llegó durante el Abierto de los Estados Unidos 2025 cuando su hermano le rapó al cero.

articles.body:
Última hora del Alcaraz - Cerúndolo, en directo

Buenos días, ya estamos aquí de nuevo. El tenis vuelve a ser protagonista en esta matinal sabatina. Carlos Alcaraz afronta su primer partido en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái. El murciano llega a la cita tras levantar el trofeo en el ATP 500 de Tokio, el tercero en una temporada marcada por su parón de 138 días por la lesión de muñeca.

Con un balance de 32 victorias y cuatro derrotas en este curso, Alcaraz tiene los cuartos de final como tope en Shanghái. Es uno de los tres Masters 1000 que le faltan en su palmarés junto al de Canadá y París. Sólo dos tenistas han conseguido todos: Djokovic, en dos ocasiones, y Sinner, que lo logró este curso tras coronar cinco seguidos con Roma como último eslabón.

Su ausencia el año pasado en Shanghái permiten a Alcaraz optar a 1.000 puntos que le ratifiquen en el Top 3 y estar más cerca de recupera el primer puesto del ranking mundial el próximo año.

Alcaraz se mide hoy a Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, número 55 de la ATP. Sólo se han enfrentado en una ocasión con victoria del murciano. Fue en la 'round robin' de las Next Gen Finals de Milán en 2021 .

articles.summary: El asturiano se impone en tres sets y
articles.body: Pablo Carreño, a sus 35 años, ha llegado con fuerza a la parte final de la temporada. Lo demuestra su clasificación este sábado, por primera vez, para la tercera ronda del Masters 1000 de Shanghái tras derrotar a Alejandro Tabilo (29), por 4-6, 7-6(2) y 6-4. El chileno tendrá pesadillas con los tenistas españoles. Y es que cuatro de sus derrotas en el presente curso han sido frente a miembros de la 'Armada'. Rafa Jódar, por dos veces, y Dani Mérida, ya le habían superado antes de que lo hiciera Carreño. El veterano jugador gijonés se las verá ahora con Felix Auger-Aliassime, cuarto cabeza de serie y uno de los involucrados en la pelea por estar en las ATP Finals de Turín. El canadiense decantó a su favor el único precedente entre ambos en las semifinales de Rotterdam, 2020. Pablo tenía que defender esta semana los 100 puntos de campeón del Ferrero Challenger de Villena. De momento, suma 50 en el TMS chino.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard displays new look in victory at Shanghai Masters as Mirra Andreeva, Qinwen Zheng make China Open final
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz seals straight-sets win over Juan Manuel Cerundolo at Shanghai Masters; Daniil Medvedev also wins; Mirra Andreeva, Qinwen Zheng make China Open final; watch WTA China Open until October 11 and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters October 7-18 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The world No 3, sporting a freshly trimmed moustache, delivered an aggressive performance to defeat Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3 6-3 and reach the third round of the ATP Masters 1000 event.

Alcaraz repeatedly surged forward with purpose during their 66-minute encounter, showcasing his deft touch to extend his winning streak to seven matches following his successful title defence in Tokyo.

"It's going to stay for the week," Alcaraz confirmed when asked about his moustache. "I always wanted to step on court at least once with a moustache.

"Before Tokyo with the team, we said, 'If I win the tournament, we all have to do the moustache and play Shanghai with it.' We're having fun with it. It came to stay."

Cerundolo, who stunned Jannik Sinner in five sets in the second round of Roland Garros this year, was seeking to become the first player to defeat both the Italian and Alcaraz in the same season since Andrey Rublev in 2024.

However, Alcaraz stuck to his attacking game plan, using Shanghai's quick court conditions to unsettle his opponent and press forward at every opportunity.

Medvedev advances at Shanghai in first match since China Open disqualification

Daniil Medvedev won his first match since being disqualified at the China Open for hitting a spectator in the eye with a ball.

Medvedev beat Jan-Lennard Struff 4-6 6-4 6-3 to reach the third round.

Medvedev, who now holds a 10-2 career edge over Struff, was disqualified from the China Open during his semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Medvedev, who apologised after the incident, saying it was an accident, lost the $285,000 prize money he would have received for making the semi-finals in Beijing.

In other early second-round matches Saturday, fourth-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime beat Camilo Ugo Carabelli 4-6 7-6 (7-1) 7-5.

No 1 Jannik Sinner withdrew from Shanghai this week when he announced he was taking the rest of 2026 off due to a right knee injury.

Andreeva reaches China Open final vs Zheng with 50th match win of season

Mirra Andreeva earned her 50th match win of the season by beating Nikola Bartunkova 6-2 6-2 to reach the final of the China Open.

The French Open champion will face home favourite Qinwen Zheng for the title on Sunday, after the latter beat Elise Mertens 7-5 6-2.

World No 5-ranked Andreeva is set to move up two spots in next week's rankings. The Russian player's 50th match win puts her level with Jessica Pegula for most on tour, according to the WTA.

The 19-year-old Andreeva had defeated Bartunkova, a 20-year-old Czech played ranked world No 34, in the third round of the US Open in their only other meeting.

articles.title: Alcaraz va a por el título de Shanghái con bigote y sin mangas
articles.standfirst: El murciano derrota en el debut del Masters 1000 a Juan Manuel Cerúndolo en dos rápidos sets
articles.summary: El murciano derrota en el debut del Masters 1000 a Juan Manuel Cerúndolo en dos rápidos sets
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha puesto este sábado la primera piedra para convertirse en el primer tenista español capaz de inscribir su nombre en el palmarés del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, torneo que nació en 2009. Carlitos, que tiene en los cuartos de 2024 su mejor actuación en certamen, superó en el debut a Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, por 6-3 y 6-3, en 66 minutos. El 78 por ciento de primeros saques fue una de las agradables claves para el número tres mundial. Cerúndolo es uno de los 14 tenistas zurdo del 'top100'. Al murciano le sienta bien ese perfil de jugador, no en vano ha decantado a su favor 41 de los 53 partidos disputados contra rivales que responden a esas características. Alcaraz sorprendió a los aficionados que se congregaron en la central cubierta del Qi Zhong con un nuevo look, con bigote, una apuesta pagada junto al resto de su equipo por el título de Tokio. "El equipo del bigote", firmó a la cámara a la conclusión. Carlitos recuperó para la ocasión la elástica Nike sin mangas de los Knicks de Nueva York que sólo había lucido el 25 de agosto, en el dobles mixto del US Open al lado de Serena Williams. Juan Manuel, consciente de que a su adversario le gusta empezar restando, ganó el sorteo y le mandó a sacar. Los dos protagonistas mantuvieron su servicio hasta el sexto juego. El argentino sumó sus primeros nueve puntos al servicio para perderlo después con un pasante de revés del campeón de siete grandes. Alcaraz había pasado al ataque en una de las superficies más rápidas del circuito. La aumentaba el techo retráctil, que se tuvo que poner como consecuencia de la lluvia. Los nueve golpes ganadores del fenómeno de El Palmar contrastaban con los dos de su víctima, muy lejos en tenis y en su ranking, el 55 del mundo. "Usando pista pequeña, cruzado y centro", le repetía Samu a su pupilo cuando ya dominaba por 4-2 en la continuación. Alcaraz, con un 18 por ciento de reveses cortados en 2026, firmaba un 43 ante el menor de los Cerúndolo. Un error no forzado con la derecha le dio el triunfo a su verdugo. El pupilo de Samuel López ha ganado los últimos 18 partidos ante adversarios del país de Cerúndolo. Su única derrota fue en el primer duelo con Federico Coria. En la tercera ronda del lunes espera al ganador del partido entre Ignacio Buse (32) y Zizou Bergs.

articles.title: Frances Tiafoe grew up inside a tennis centre where his father worked: The remarkable journey from sleeping on couches to competing on the biggest courts in tennis history
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring journey of Frances Tiafoe, who transformed his humble beginnings at a tennis center into a remarkable tennis career, becoming a top ATP player and US Open semifinalist. Learn about his family's sacrifices and his rise through the ranks.
articles.body: Frances Tiafoe’s professional career is closely connected to the Junior Tennis Champions Center in College Park, Maryland, where his father, Frances Tiafoe Sr., worked in maintenance. The facility was not simply a place where the young American learned tennis; it became the setting for much of his childhood, giving him extraordinary access to courts and coaches while his family worked to build a life in the United States.Years later, that unusual beginning has become part of the larger story behind Tiafoe’s success. The American progressed from junior standout to ATP champion, broke into the world's top 10 and established himself as a regular presence deep into major tournaments, and his journey reached another important chapter in 2026, when he won his biggest career title in Halle and reached his third US Open semifinal.Frances Tiafoe’s remarkable childhood inside a Maryland tennis centerTiafoe’s connection with JTCC began at an exceptionally young age. His father was among the workers involved in building the facility before eventually becoming its head of maintenance. Frances and his twin brother, Franklin, spent substantial time there while their parents worked, making the tennis centre a central part of their everyday lives.The family’s circumstances were far removed from the polished environment normally associated with professional tennis. Tiafoe Sr., an immigrant from Sierra Leone, worked long hours at the centre. Earlier accounts of Tiafoe’s childhood describe the family staying in a small room at the facility, with the brothers sleeping there while their father worked.That arrangement gave Frances something few aspiring players receive: constant exposure to tennis. According to the ATP Tour, he began hitting balls against a wall at three alongside Franklin and trained at JTCC as a child. The centre effectively became both a workplace for his father and an early development ground for the future professional.Tiafoe was also surrounded by coaches and players from the beginning. His access to the courts meant that tennis was not an occasional after-school activity but an environment that shaped his daily routine. The Washington Post described him as being essentially raised at the centre, reflecting just how deeply the facility influenced his early development.Frances Tiafoe’s family shaped his tennis journeyTiafoe’s family story provides important context for his rise. His parents moved from Sierra Leone to the United States in 1996, and his father eventually found employment at JTCC after being involved in the facility’s construction. His mother, Alphina, also played an important role in supporting Frances and Franklin while working and helping with their education.For Tiafoe, the family’s sacrifices became part of his motivation. His father’s demanding schedule placed the young twins close to the tennis courts, while Frances gradually showed that he possessed an unusual ability to absorb the game around him.The combination of opportunity and determination became particularly visible during his teenage years. At 15, Tiafoe won the 2013 Orange Bowl boys’ 18s title, becoming the youngest champion in the event’s history at that time. The achievement elevated his profile among American junior players and demonstrated that the teenager could compete well beyond his age group.His development also required a demanding balance between education and tennis. Contemporary reporting showed Tiafoe spending long days at JTCC, combining schoolwork with several hours of training. That routine illustrated how early his life became organised around the goal of becoming a professional player.Frances Tiafoe turned adversity into stardomTiafoe’s transition to the ATP Tour eventually produced the breakthrough his junior career had promised. In 2018, at only 20, he won his first ATP title at the Delray Beach Open. The victory was especially meaningful because he defeated his childhood idol Juan Martin del Potro during the tournament.The American continued developing into one of the most recognisable players on tour. He reached his first Grand Slam quarterfinal at the 2019 Australian Open before producing an even bigger breakthrough at the 2022 US Open.At Flushing Meadows that year, Tiafoe defeated Rafael Nadal in the quarterfinals and became the first American man since Andy Roddick in 2006 to reach the US Open semifinals, and the victory over Nadal represented one of the defining moments of his career and brought global attention to the story behind his rise.Tiafoe returned to the US Open semifinals in 2024, and his consistency at the tournament became a defining part of his Grand Slam resume, and he also reached the Cincinnati Masters final in 2024, showing that his success was not limited to New York.His 2026 season added another significant chapter, after making changes to his coaching setup and approach following the 2025 season, Tiafoe enjoyed a strong resurgence. He won the Halle title, his biggest trophy at the time, reached another Cincinnati Masters final and advanced to the US Open semifinals for the third time. His run in New York also secured a return to the ATP top 10 and a new career-high ranking of No. 8.Career milestoneFrances Tiafoe2013Youngest Orange Bowl boys’ 18s champion at 152014Won Easter Bowl boys’ 18s title2018Won first ATP title in Delray Beach2019Reached Australian Open quarterfinal2022Reached US Open semifinal after beating Rafael Nadal2023Reached career-high No. 102024Reached US Open semifinal and Cincinnati Masters final2026Won Halle title and reached US Open semifinal2026 ranking milestoneCareer-high No. 8The contrast between Tiafoe’s childhood and his present position in tennis makes the journey particularly striking. The player who once spent much of his childhood around a Maryland tennis facility now competes regularly on the sport’s biggest stages.His story also extends beyond results. Tiafoe received the Arthur Ashe Humanitarian Award in 2020 and has supported initiatives connected with youth tennis and charitable causes. In 2024, he donated $50,000 through his charitable fund with the USTA Foundation during JTCC’s 25th-anniversary celebrations.That connection to JTCC has therefore remained meaningful long after Tiafoe left the junior ranks. The centre that once represented his family’s workplace and his earliest tennis education eventually became part of the foundation of a professional career that has reached the ATP top 10 and three US Open semifinals.Tiafoe’s path remains a powerful example of how access, family sacrifice, relentless training and opportunity can combine to change an athlete’s trajectory. From sleeping in basic quarters at the facility where his father worked to standing under the lights at Arthur Ashe Stadium, his career has transformed the circumstances of his childhood into one of American tennis’ most compelling modern stories.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A qué hora es el Alcaraz - Bergs: horario y dónde ver en TV y online la tercera ronda del Masters 1000 de Shanghái
articles.standfirst: El tenista de El Palmar se impuso en el único precedente en los octavos de Tokio 2025
articles.summary: El tenista de El Palmar se impuso en el único precedente en los octavos de Tokio 2025
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, a sus 23 años, ha debutado este sábado con victoria en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái gracias a un doble 6-3 ante Juan Manuel Cerúndolo. Este lunes buscará un lugar en los octavos ante el belga Zizou Bergs, el 39 de las listas. Este ha dado buena cuenta del peruano Ignacio Buse (32), por 6-0 y 6-3, en 65 minutos, uno menos del que necesitó el murciano para derrotar al pequeño de los Cerúndolo. Alcaraz se impuso a Bergs en el único precedente entre ambos en los octavos del Open 500 de Tokio 2025. Carlitos tiene en los cuartos de 2024 su mejor resultado en el TMS chino que se perdió en la pasada edición por fatiga. El partido de la tercera ronda del Masters 1000 de Shanghái entre Carlos Alcaraz y Zizou Bergs se disputará este lunes 12 de octubre en la central del Qi Zhong, en un horario todavía por confirmar. La tercera ronda del Masters 1000 de Shanghái entre Carlos Alcaraz y Zizou Bergs podrá seguirse en España a través de Movistar+, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: La derrota de Pedro Martínez deja sin españoles la final del Ferrero Challenger de Villena
articles.standfirst: El valenciano cedió su semifinal con el serbio Laslo Djere en dos rápidos sets
articles.summary: El valenciano cedió su semifinal con Daniil Glinka en dos rápidos sets
articles.body: El tenis masculino español se ha quedado este sábado sin la posibilidad de lograr por quinta vez el trofeo del Ferrero & Forty Challenger de Villena. Pedro Martínez, el único miembro de la Armada presente en las semifinales, ha cedido a manos del serbio Laslo Djere, por 6-4 y 6-2. La otra semifinal la ganó Daniil Glinka ante Jack Pinnington Jones, por 3-6, 7-6(6) y 6-2. Cabe recordar que Pablo Carreño es el último campeón del certamen que reparte 100 puntos al campeón. El asturiano juega estos días en Shanghái donde ha alcanzado la tercera ronda del Masters 1000. Martínez, cuarto cabeza de serie del cuadro, se queda lejos del 'top100' mundial, que da el billete directo para la próxima edición del Open de Australia. El valenciano, que empezó la semana en el puesto 130, escala seis posiciones.

articles.title: Former Tennis Australia chief Craig Tiley sold his Melbourne beachfront home for $7.35 million after buying it in 2022; the sale left him with a $5.75 million loss
articles.summary: Craig Tiley’s Aspendale home has found a buyer, but the price was well below what he paid for the property in 2022.
articles.body: Craig Tiley’s Aspendale home has found a buyer, but the price was well below what he paid for the property in 2022. The beachfront home at 73 Nepean Highway, Melbourne, was sold for $7.35 million, according to a report by the Herald Sun. The former tennis chief bought the home in 2022 for about $13.1 million, leaving him with a loss of $5.75 million.Aspendale home sale ends in lossThe timing of the Aspendale home sale is crucial. In February, Tiley announced he would leave his role as chief executive of Tennis Australia to take up the top job at the US Tennis Association. The following month, he listed the house for $11.5 million. The asking price later fell to $8.75 million, and the sale was confirmed in late September.The listing agents remained tight-lipped about the final figure. Until the records emerged, no party associated with the sale had disclosed how much the house had changed hands for. This is common in a market where many buyers and sellers prefer discretion.However, Tiley’s loss is significant. The $5.75 million figure is only part of the bill. Tiley also paid $831,500 in stamp duty, calculated on the original purchase price. Add that to the loss, and the total comes to roughly $6.58 million. That loss works out at about $4,070 a day. Without the stamp duty, the daily figure is closer to $3,560. Either way, the sale resulted in a loss for the tennis chief.Inside the houseLocated at 73 Nepean Highway, Aspendale, the property sits on approximately 1,998 sq m. According to the listing, the property has “breathtaking panoramic views across Port Phillip Bay and direct access onto the sand, placing the beach quite literally at your doorstep”. The house sits on one of the most exclusive and secluded stretches of coastline.The home has four bedrooms, four bathrooms and three living rooms. It also has a floodlit tennis court, a heated pool and a spa. The house comes with a four-car garage. The kitchen is fitted with gourmet Gaggenau appliances and includes a butler’s pantry and a wine fridge.“Step straight out of your gate for a morning swim, paddleboard, or simply take in the ever-changing seascape as the bay comes alive with dolphins, kite surfers and spectacular sunsets,” the listing says. There is also a private upper-level retreat with a balcony, dressing room and en-suite bathroom.According to the listing, the estate’s outdoor spaces have the feel of “a private coastal sanctuary”.Tiley’s house is not the only Aspendale property on the market. RT Edgar Bayside’s Joe Doyle is handling the campaign for 20 Bowman St, a five-bedroom home with an 11-car basement garage and a beachfront pool. It is priced between $9.5 million and $9.9 million.Cameron Howe of One Agency Longbeach described the local market as a pyramid. Entry-level homes are still changing hands as buyers seek affordability and a coastal lifestyle. “As you climb the pyramid, the fish get fewer and the pain gets higher, particularly for vendors who purchased in the past couple of years,” Mr Howe told the outlet.“Correctly priced properties are still attracting buyers and moving, particularly in beachside suburbs where the coastal lifestyle, strong local and state government investment and cosmopolitan dining scene in places like Mordialloc continue to hold appeal, but buyers are getting pickier with the choice a spring market brings.”Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision?
